title: Saved Allen visual response spectra show a compression crossover between VISl and VISp in two recording methods
abstract: We tested whether higher mouse visual areas have more concentrated response spectra at every dimension count. We used published aggregate cvPCA spectra for 118 images, with 50 draws of 300 units or cells per area, from 32 Neuropixels mice and 193 two-photon mice. VISl and VISp had crossing cumulative variance profiles in both methods. VISl had larger participation dimensions (28.45 versus 25.49; 33.81 versus 29.31), but needed fewer dimensions for 90 percent of variance (50 versus 52; 59 versus 62). Crossings occurred in 92.36 and 97.92 percent of saved unit-draw pairs. A Gaussian surrogate with equal total signal power changed its VISl–VISp information order with noise level. This reversal depended on the spectral tail. Thus a hierarchy trend in fitted decay does not imply one full-profile compression order. The analysis does not refute the original slope result. Limits: aggregate noisy cvPCA estimates, exploratory pair selection, no new mouse-level intervals, and no measured task or information outcome. Code, licensed aggregate inputs, exact hashes, proofs and sensitivity results are included.

display.caption: VISl and VISp have crossing compression profiles in both recording methods. Bands show unit-draw variation, not mouse confidence intervals. The Gaussian information reversal is a model result.
